text: The review is served by the published outcome operation PATCH /api/recovery/deviation/v1/deviations/{deviationId} (API-S8-002) with the DeviationOutcome request and the Deviation answer of TSD S8 T-A.2, and the queue read of SCR-08 carries the placeholder until its own operation is published.
why: TSD S8 T-A.1 publishes no read operation for the queue and the FSD names no operation for the review, while T-A.2 already declares the operation that records an outcome.
read: The suffix and the element names are copied from T-A.1 and T-A.2 onto the service base of DP-13; the review is the step of that operation that carries the outcome; a queue read is not invented and is written as the placeholder.
confirm: Solution architect and the owner of the gateway-bff composite route
impact: None on other services: the raise step keeps API-S8-001 and the review adds no path.

text: The outcome the review records maps to a DEVIATION row as follows: RETURNED to R-DEV-09 and DEV_RESOLVED for codes X1 and X7, RE_ROUTED to R-DEV-10 and DEV_REROUTE for X2 or to R-DEV-22 and DEV_REROUTE where no next step is named, and CASE_ENDED to R-DEV-11 and CASE_ENDED where insurance clears the balance.
why: TSD S8 T3.2 publishes the three values and T4 publishes the four rows, but no source states which value drives which row, and FSD S8 A2.17 names no rule.
read: The mapping is read from the to-states the rules name against the outcome words; it is held in reference data and the code carries no branch on a literal; an outcome that matches no row is refused with MSG-GEN-001 and changes nothing.
impact: A reporting query on the deviation outcome reads the same three values in every environment.

text: No requirement ID is cited: the traceability row of both stories carries the placeholder of CG-B2-S8-008-2 until a REQ row names FEAT-DVF-08.
why: TSD S8 T8 maps REQ-DVH-001 to REQ-DVH-011 and REQ-S8-001 to REQ-S8-007 to FEAT-DVH-01 and FEAT-DVF-01 only, and no row of the table names the review.
read: The requirement is stated by FEAT-DVF-08 of the FSD and the BRD, which are the feature sources; no REQ ID is invented and the traceability table names the gap instead.
confirm: Business analyst, S8, and the RTM owner
impact: The RTM shows the review unnumbered until the requirement is issued; no test loses its trace.

text: The review writes the outcome of the deviation and sends the case move; it does not set cleared_at, does not lift the contact stop, does not resume the stage clock and publishes no DeviationCleared, which stay with the clearance feature FEAT-DVH-06 and its R-DEV-18.
why: FEAT-DVH-06 Clear a deviation and resume the timers owns the clearance, the stop and the clock, and FEAT-DVF-08 names none of them; the two overlap on the outcome field.
read: The outcome column DF-CAS-045 is this step's; cleared_at DF-CAS-044, contact_stop DF-CAS-043 and the paused state DF-CAS-041 are read only here; the event set of TSD S8 T5.3 is left to the step that clears.
confirm: Business analyst, S8, and the owner of the clearance story
impact: A case stays on hold until the clearance step runs, so no stop is lifted by a review alone.

text: The review is a synchronous service step: it declares no Temporal workflow, no activity, no Schedule, no Quartz row and no shared job table, and the package is read as data rather than evaluated through an embedded Drools kit.
why: TSD S8 T4 publishes the DEVIATION state machine and no workflow, FSD S8 A2.17.4.4 declares no background event, and DP-04 and DP-10 are not in the plan's pattern set for this key.
read: The step runs inside the request; the stage that hosts it is the case workflow of rwb-case; the Quartz job of the module belongs to the stage clock and the clearance and becomes the Schedule of those stories.
confirm: Solution architect and the Temporal platform owner
impact: One fewer workflow to register; a later decision to run the review as a workflow adds it without a change to section 12.1.

text: The case read, the case-move answer and the package read are consumed as published contracts and answered by their fakes on Day 1, even though the plan's contract-dependency row is None.
why: The review reads the case state and the package and answers the move, so the three rows exist in fact, while the work package fixes the C row as empty and no source publishes the operation names.
read: One hop, 2 s timeout, a breaker and no retry of its own per row; the operation names carry the placeholder; the rows are class C and block no build.
confirm: Solution architect, rwb-case and rwb-decision contract owners
impact: The service builds on Day 1 without a live P3 or P7 and the C row stays as the plan fixed it.

text: The service facts are taken from Template and Rules v1 R4, FSD S8 v3 and TSD S8 v2 because the S8 context pack and the S8 module extracts are absent: schema and login rwb_deviation, base /api/recovery/deviation/v1, topic rwb.deviation.events.v1, queue rwb-deviation and Java package th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.deviation.
why: The work package names the context pack as the authority for service facts and the file does not exist in this workspace, so the same facts have to come from a lower source in the precedence list.
read: The naming rule of R4 is mechanical on the short name deviation; the ownership is read from TSD S8 T3.3 and T5.2; the service wave of Arch v5 is 2 and the story wave 4 comes from the W-MAP of EP07.
confirm: Solution architect, when the context pack is issued
impact: A correction of a naming fact would touch section 12.1 and section 13 of both stories and no test.

text: The operation declares the Case record right U that TSD S8 T-A.1 gives it, and the entitlement of the review role is left as a placeholder: the right the risk and model risk officer needs to record a review is not stated, because T6.1 gives RW-RISK, RW-CONDUCT and RW-COE right R while the FSD makes the risk officer the primary role.
why: A conflict between the FSD role table and the TSD rights matrix cannot be settled by the story and no source gives the right the forum member holds on the review.
read: The contract keeps the right of the operation; the story states the entitlement as the placeholder and does not grant a right the matrix does not give; a role without right U is refused with MSG-P4-002 as the matrix requires.
confirm: Business lead, S8, and the access owner of rwb-access
impact: Until the right is confirmed the review may be refused for the primary role, and the refusal is the matrix's.

text: Both stories keep wave 4 from the W-MAP of EP07 and raise no wave conflict, although Arch v5 puts rwb-deviation in wave 2.
why: Template and Rules R5.6 raises a conflict only where the W-MAP wave is earlier than the service wave, and here the story wave is later.
read: The release date 31 May 2027 is copied unchanged and marked tentative; no date is raised as a gap.
impact: The service delivers its review step in wave 4 with the rest of EP07.
